description: REQ-25/PROP-26's malformed-ratio fail-closed guarantee is proven for exactly 4 shapes (missing, N=0, negative, non-integer via letters), but a realistic 5th malformed shape — a digit-only ratio string with a leading zero (e.g. ARTICLE_MODEB_RATIO='08', '09', or '1-in-08') — is accepted as 'valid' by both regexes in run.sh's _modeb_ratio_n() (lines 98 '^1-in-([0-9]+)$' and 100 '^[0-9]+$'), yet is NOT a value bash's own arithmetic evaluator treats safely: bash's $(( )) and the numeric '[ -eq ]' comparison both parse a leading-zero digit string as an OCTAL literal, and '08'/'09' are invalid octal (digit 8/9 does not exist in base 8), raising a runtime 'value too great for base' error. This exact input shape is not present in ANY of: (a) REQ-25's 4 named cases, (b) test-prop26a's 4 cases ('', '0', '-3', 'three'), (c) test-prop26b's mutation sequence ('1', '0', '2'), or (d) test-prop24b's 6 fault-injection scenarios ('-1', '0', 'abc', missing, valid+AUTONOMY-off, 'garbage-not-a-number' counter). The SAME hazard applies to the wake-counter file (run.sh line 120, _modeb_next_wake_count): its sanitizer 'case "$cur" in (''|*[!0-9]*) cur=0 ;; esac' only rejects non-digit characters, so a counter file externally corrupted to a leading-zero value (e.g. '08') passes the sanitizer unchanged and then hits the same '$((cur + 1))' octal-parse hazard at line 121 — precisely the 'deliberately-corrupted/adversarial ... wake-counter value' class CRIT-404 explicitly claims to be resilient against, but this specific corruption shape was never exercised. REQ-25's own text requires 'a div/mod-by-zero or parse error SHALL be caught and treated identically to "ratio says Mode A"' as an explicit, deliberate handling requirement — the current code has NO explicit catch for this class of error; it relies on incidental bash short-circuit behavior (an erroring $(( )) expansion inside 'if [ $((wake_n % ratio_n)) -eq 0 ]' most likely evaluates the surrounding [ ] as false, which HAPPENS to leave effective_mode at its default 'A') rather than a deliberate, tested guard. Because this is genuinely untested, the actual runtime behavior on the reviewer's/production bash version is UNVERIFIED by this sprint's own test suite, and at minimum it will emit raw bash interpreter error text ('bash: line N: 08: value too great for base') to run.sh's stderr on every affected wake in production -- for a safety gate that is the ONLY thing preventing an unattended, irreversible, monetized publish action from firing more often than intended, an unverified/untested failure mode is not an acceptable evidentiary state.

evidence.snippet:
elif [[ "$raw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  n="$raw"
...
if [ "$n" -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  return 1
fi
...
if [ $((wake_n % ratio_n)) -eq 0 ]; then
  effective_mode="B"
fi

recommendation: Reject non-canonical numeric shapes before they ever reach bash arithmetic: require '^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$' (no leading zero except the literal '0' itself, which is already rejected as N=0) instead of the current '^[0-9]+$', apply the same canonical-shape check to the wake-counter sanitizer at line 120, and add a distinct test case (e.g. test-prop26a case 5: ARTICLE_MODEB_RATIO='08') proving it fails closed to Mode A the same way the other 4 documented cases do, plus a companion case for a leading-zero wake-counter file value.
